glosses: To possess, own.

examples.text: I have a house and a car.

glosses: To hold, as something at someone's disposal.

examples.text: Look what I have here—a frog I found on the street!
Do you have the key?

glosses: To include as a part, ingredient, or feature.

examples.text: The stove has a handle. The shirt has sleeves.
The words cow and dog have three letters.
A government has three branches: the executive, legislative, and judicial.
The movie has lots of action.

glosses: Used to state the existence or presence of someone in a specified relationship with the subject.

examples.text: I have two sisters.
She doesn’t have any friends.
I have a really mean boss.

glosses: To consume or use up (a particular substance or resource, especially food or drink).

examples.text: I have breakfast at six o'clock.
You've already had five drinks!
She's had more than enough time already.

glosses: To undertake or perform (an action or activity).

examples.text: Can I have a look at that?
He's having a tantrum about it.
I’m going to have a bath now.
Let’s have a game of tiddlywinks.

glosses: To be scheduled to attend, undertake or participate in.

examples.text: What class do you have right now? I have English.
Fred won’t be able to come to the party; he has a meeting that day.
I have a lot of work to do.

glosses: To experience, go through, undergo.

examples.text: We had a hard year last year, with the locust swarms and all that.
He had surgery on his hip yesterday.
I’m having the time of my life!
I hope you have a wonderful birthday.

glosses: To be afflicted with, suffer from.

examples.text: He had a cold last week.

glosses: Used in forming the perfect aspect.

examples.text: I have already eaten today.
Mom's gone real mad, she has.

glosses: Used as an interrogative verb before a pronoun to form a tag question, echoing a previous use of 'have' as an auxiliary verb or, in certain cases, main verb. (For further discussion, see the appendix English tag questions.)

examples.text: They haven’t eaten dinner yet, have they?
Your wife hasn’t been reading that nonsense, has she?
He has some money, hasn’t he?

glosses: See have to.

examples.text: I have to go.

glosses: To give birth to.

glosses: To obtain.

examples.text: The substance you describe can't be had at any price.

examples.text: He’s always bragging about how many women he’s had.

glosses: To accept as a romantic partner.

examples.text: Despite my protestations of love, she would not have me.

glosses: To cause to, by a command, request or invitation.

examples.text: They had me feed their dog while they were out of town.

glosses: To cause to be.

examples.text: He had him arrested for trespassing.

examples.text: The hospital had several patients contract pneumonia last week.

glosses: To depict as being.

examples.text: I could have him!

examples.text: I have no German.

glosses: To allow; to tolerate.

glosses: Se procurer, obtenir quelque chose.

examples.text: Puis-je avoir la parole ?

glosses: Tromper, berner, leurrer quelqu’un.

examples.text: J’ai l’impression que je me suis fait avoir.

examples.text: « Autant j’aime qu’une femme me plaise, autant il m’est impossible d’estimer une femme que j’ai eue. »

examples.text: Oui, j’ai mon amie qui m’attend.

glosses: Auxiliaire servant à former les temps composés, signifiant le passé, la complétion ou l’expérience.
target_senses.note: Certains verbes demandent être comme auxiliaire. En français moderne, le passé composé est beaucoup plus courant que le passé simple

examples.text: Ça humait l’accord du participe passé avec l’auxiliaire avoir quand le complément d’objet est placé sans devant derrière.

glosses: Ce que possède un individu.

examples.text: Pour les hommes de Chronos, l’avoir d’un passé ne saurait être analogue à l’avoir des choses ; bien que mort et irretrouvable, ou plutôt parce que mort et irretrouvable, notre passé nous possède plus que nous ne le possédons.

glosses: Ensemble des biens et richesses appartenant à un individu ou à une personne morale, possession.

examples.text: M. Donnet, son père, a été maire de Caen pendant toute la durée du gouvernement de Juillet. Pourchassé sous le second Empire il perdra tout son avoir.
Le 26 juillet : Nasser nationalise le Canal de Suez et décide de geler tous les avoirs de la Compagnie universelle du canal de Suez.
Par la nature de leurs richesses : ces bourgeois fortunés sont des « terriers » comme on dit à Lyon ; ils ont investi une grande part de leur avoir dans des fonds.

glosses: Somme d’argent qu’un établissement commercial (banque, entreprise, etc.) doit à son client, solde créditeur.

examples.text: Les plaignants souhaitent poursuivre la compagnie aérienne canadienne qui a choisi d’offrir à ses clients américains des avoirs pour des voyages futurs et non des remboursements, a indiqué CTV News.
Vous avez un avoir de cent euros.

glosses: Le fait de posséder, par opposition au fait d'être ou de faire.

examples.text: Avoir ou être? La civilisation de consommation, inhumaine et aberrante, nous impose dès l'enfance la loi de l'avoir donc de la souffrance.
